digest.headline: Wall Street equities rallied and Treasury yields slid as Waller delivered dovish remarks.

lede.b: The S&P 500 index, which is a group of stocks representing big American companies, went up by 1.1%. At the same time, US Treasury yields, which are the interest payments the government gives to people who lend it money, dropped. This drop happened after a Federal Reserve official named Waller made remarks that suggested interest rates might not go up further. Lower yields make borrowing money cheaper for companies and regular people. Investors are now waiting for the upcoming non-farm payrolls data release, which tells us how many jobs the country added.
lede.i: Wall Street indices advanced in unison, pushing the S&P 500 up by 1.1% during the trading session. US Treasury yields slid across fixed-income markets following dovish remarks from Waller. This compression in yields lowers borrowing costs throughout the economy. Market participants now turn their focus to the upcoming non-farm payrolls data release.
lede.a: Major US equity benchmarks advanced synchronously, driving the S&P 500 up 1.1% on broad buying. US Treasury yields declined across the curve following dovish commentary from Waller, reducing fixed-income borrowing costs. Market positioning now pivots entirely to the incoming non-farm payrolls release to reprice terminal rate expectations.

items.b: The S&P 500 index went up by 1.1% as investors pushed up valuations across the board.
items.i: The S&P 500 closed up 1.1% as broad equity benchmarks advanced in unison.
items.a: The S&P 500 gained 1.1% amid synchronized equity appreciation and broad valuation support.

items.b: Bank of England officials warned that government demands to finance fiscal deficits threaten central bank independence.
items.i: Bank of England officials stated that government demands to finance fiscal deficits threaten central bank independence.
items.a: Bank of England officials flagged sovereign pressures to finance fiscal deficits as the primary risk to central bank independence.

items.b: The DAX index rose by 0.65% to reach 26,003.32 points, ending a three-day losing streak.
items.i: The DAX index reached 26,003.32 points, securing a 0.65% gain that snapped a three-session losing streak.
items.a: The DAX rose 0.65% to 26,003.32 points, breaking a three-session losing run as European bourses advanced.

items.b: The Japanese yen traded near the 155 range while government budget requests hit a record 143 trillion yen.
items.i: The Japanese yen traded near the 155 level amid a potential carry trade reversal.
items.a: The Japanese yen hovered near 155 against the dollar as potential carry trade unwind pressures drove futures toward their steepest weekly drop since June.

thread.b: Central banks and currency markets moved in response to shifting economic expectations. The Japanese yen climbed while US Treasury yields dropped following remarks from officials.
thread.i: Central bank policy expectations drove currency and fixed-income movements. Declining US yields contrasted with yen strength driven by carry trade unwind speculation.
thread.a: Cross-border capital flows responded to shifting monetary policy trajectories and fiscal pressures. Sovereign debt yields compressed in the US while currency adjustments reflected evolving carry trade dynamics in Japan.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Wall Street rallies and Treasury yields fall

stories.t: Wall Street Indices Post Gains
stories.b: The S&P 500 index rose by 1.1% on Wall Street. An index is a group of shares tracked together to measure market performance. All three major US stock indexes moved higher during the session. Shares gained ground as investor sentiment improved across the board.
stories.i: The S&P 500 closed up 1.1% as major indices rallied together. Equity benchmarks advanced in unison during the trading session. Broad buying lifted valuations across the board.
stories.a: The S&P 500 advanced 1.1% in a synchronized rally across major benchmarks. Equity indices captured upward momentum as risk appetite expanded. Broad participation underpinned the advance across sectors.

stories.t: Treasury Yields Slide Following Remarks
stories.b: US Treasury yields dropped after comments from Waller. A Treasury yield is the return the government pays people who lend it money by buying its bonds, which are like official IOUs. Lower yields mean the cost of borrowing has gone down. Traders now await the non-farm payrolls data release.
stories.i: US Treasury yields fell following dovish remarks from Waller. Falling yields reflect lower borrowing costs across fixed-income markets. Market participants shifted their attention to the upcoming non-farm payrolls data release.
stories.a: US Treasury yields declined in response to Waller's dovish signalling. The curve compressed as duration bids absorbed the shift in policy expectations. Attention immediately pivoted to the impending non-farm payrolls print.

politics.b: There are no political updates available in the current reports.
politics.i: No political developments were reported in the session.
politics.a: No sovereign or legislative updates were logged in the data.

timeline: Puma Biotechnology reports inducement awards under Nasdaq listing rule.
Waller delivers dovish commentary affecting Treasury yields.
Major US stock indexes close up with the S&P 500 gaining 1.1%.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank of England defends its independence

stories.t: Fiscal Deficits Threaten Central Bank Independence
stories.b: Bank of England officials stated that government demands to finance fiscal deficits pose the greatest threat to central bank independence. A central bank manages a country's money and interest rates. It operates separately from the government so it can keep prices stable. Government spending demands can pressure these institutions to print money or keep borrowing costs artificially low. Bank of England officials highlighted this risk.
stories.i: Bank of England officials stated that government demands to finance fiscal deficits pose the greatest threat to central bank independence. Fiscal deficits occur when public spending exceeds government revenue, requiring sovereign debt issuance. Direct financing pressures undermine monetary authority and credibility. Bank of England officials highlighted this risk.
stories.a: Bank of England officials identified sovereign financing demands for fiscal deficits as the primary risk to central bank operational independence. Monetising public debt or accommodating fiscal expansion compromises monetary policy reaction functions and anchors. Bank of England officials highlighted this risk.

politics.b: Bank of England officials stated that government demands to finance fiscal deficits pose the greatest threat to central bank independence. Bank of England officials highlighted this risk.
politics.i: Bank of England officials stated that government demands to finance fiscal deficits pose the greatest threat to central bank independence. Bank of England officials highlighted this risk.
politics.a: Bank of England officials stated that government demands to finance fiscal deficits pose the greatest threat to central bank independence. Bank of England officials highlighted this risk.

timeline: Bank of England officials warn over fiscal deficit financing demands.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: Frankfurt equities rise and index membership shifts

stories.t: Frankfurt Equities Snap Losing Streak
stories.b: An index is a group of shares whose overall value is tracked to see how a stock market is doing. The DAX index climbed to 26,003.32 points. This advance broke a three-day sequence of declines for German stocks. European markets gained ground as risk appetite improved. The DAX closed up 0.65% on the trading day.
stories.i: An index measures the performance of a basket of equities. The DAX index reached 26,003.32 points. This move ended a three-session losing streak for German equities. European bourses rose alongside broader improvements in market risk appetite. The DAX finished the session with a 0.65% gain.
stories.a: The benchmark equity index printed at 26,003.32 points, terminating a three-day bearish correction. European risk sentiment recovered across regional desks, driving local betas higher. Closing metrics confirmed a 0.65% advance for the DAX. Price action reflected broad-based buying rather than sector-specific catalysts.

stories.t: STOXX Alters Blue-Chip Roster
stories.b: STOXX is a company that manages lists of important company shares. It announced regular updates to these lists. Ströer will now replace Hugo Boss in the MDax index. The main DAX index list stays exactly the same. These changes affect which shares large investment funds hold.
stories.i: STOXX announced scheduled changes to its equity indices. Ströer replaces Hugo Boss in the MDax index. Meanwhile, the main DAX index constituents remain unchanged following the review. Index adjustments typically trigger rebalancing flows among passive institutional funds tracking these benchmarks.
stories.a: STOXX executed scheduled portfolio adjustments across its blue-chip index hierarchy. Ströer enters the MDax index, displacing Hugo Boss. The flagship DAX index composition remained untouched in this review cycle. Active and passive asset managers adjusted portfolio weights to match the new index constituents.

politics.b: Official sources provided no updates on government policies or political events today.
politics.i: No political developments or policy announcements were reported during the session.
politics.a: No macroeconomic policy shifts or sovereign developments crossed the wires during the session.

timeline: STOXX announces index adjustments including Ströer replacing Hugo Boss in the MDax.
The DAX index closes 0.65% higher at 26,003.32 points.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Yen strength and record budget requests

stories.t: Yen climbs toward August highs
stories.b: The Japanese yen climbs to the 155 range. Traders talk about a carry trade reversal. This means investors are paying back loans they took in cheap currencies. The currency hits its strongest week in a month.
stories.i: The Japanese yen trades near the 155 range amid speculation of a carry trade reversal. This currency movement drives Japanese futures toward their steepest weekly drop since the end of June. Bond yields fall as the currency strengthens on expectations of central bank action.
stories.a: The Japanese yen strengthens into the 155 range alongside active carry trade unwinding. Japanese futures head for their steepest weekly decline since the end of June as the currency rallies. Simultaneously, domestic bond yields fall as market participants price in imminent monetary tightening.

stories.t: Government budget requests reach record total
stories.b: The Japanese government faces a total of 143 trillion yen in budget requests for the fiscal year 2027. This sets a brand new record for state spending demands. Ministries submit these initial figures to the administration.
stories.i: Japanese government budget requests for fiscal year 2027 hit a record 143 trillion yen. State ministries submit these figures to the administration for review. This total marks the highest level of initial funding demands recorded by the government.
stories.a: Japanese fiscal year 2027 budget requests reach a record 143 trillion yen. Government ministries submit these preliminary expenditure figures for administrative evaluation. The total establishes a new peak for initial state funding demands.

stories.t: SoftBank prices large bond coupon
stories.b: SoftBank Group prices its 1 trillion yen bond with a coupon of 4.75%. A coupon is the regular interest payment a company gives to people who buy its bonds. The lead underwriter confirms the final terms for the massive debt sale.
stories.i: SoftBank Group sets the coupon on its 1 trillion yen bond at 4.75%. The lead underwriter announces the final pricing details for the debt issuance. This transaction represents a major corporate borrowing operation in the domestic market.
stories.a: SoftBank Group prices its 1 trillion yen bond offering with a 4.75% coupon. The lead underwriter confirms the final yield structure for the debt vehicle. This issuance constitutes a major corporate debt placement in the local fixed-income market.

politics.b: The UK is told to change how it buys military equipment to cut out parts made in China. Japanese ministries ask for 143 trillion yen in the fiscal year 2027 budget.
politics.i: The UK faces pressure to overhaul military procurement in order to eliminate China-made parts. Meanwhile, Japanese ministries submit record budget requests totaling 143 trillion yen for fiscal year 2027.
politics.a: Proposals urge the UK to restructure military procurement to eliminate China-sourced components. Concurrently, Japanese government ministries file initial fiscal year 2027 budget requests reaching a record 143 trillion yen.

timeline: SoftBank Group sets its 1 trillion yen bond coupon at 4.75%.

China.label: China
China.sub: Bank deposits grow as firms post financial results

stories.t: China's Big Six Banks Add Time Deposits
stories.b: China's largest six lenders added $845 billion in time deposits. Time deposits are savings locked in a bank for a set period. This happened despite record-low interest rates.
stories.i: China's six largest banks accumulated $845 billion in new time deposits. Savers committed funds to these products despite record-low interest rates across the sector.
stories.a: China's six largest banks pulled in $845 billion of new time deposits. Depositors locked in capital despite record-low yields prevailing across the banking system.

stories.t: NIO Narrows First-Half Losses
stories.b: Electric vehicle maker NIO narrowed its first-half loss by 90%. William Li leads the company through this tough period. The firm reported its financial results for the half-year period.
stories.i: NIO reduced its first-half net loss by 90%. William Li steered the electric vehicle maker through a difficult market phase. The company released its interim financial metrics.
stories.a: NIO slashed its first-half net loss by 90%. William Li navigated the electric vehicle manufacturer through severe margin compression. The firm published its interim earnings report.

politics.b: Pacific islands leaders expressed concern over a missile launch by China. The UK was urged to remove China-made parts from military equipment.
politics.i: Pacific islands leaders voiced anxiety regarding a missile launch by China. Meanwhile, the UK faced calls to strip China-made components from its military procurement supply chains.
politics.a: Pacific islands leaders registered formal concern over a missile launch conducted by China. British authorities faced renewed pressure to excise China-made parts from military procurement channels.

timeline: 3 Sep
Chinese Yuan positions and reflation risks discussed by BNY
4 Sep
China's big six banks reported $845 billion in new time deposits

India.label: India
India.sub: Rupee rises to 10-week high and RBI sets repo auction

stories.t: Rupee reaches 10-week high on inflows
stories.b: The Indian Rupee is the money used in India. It just went up in value by 0.5% against the US dollar. Strong foreign money coming into the country caused this rise. The currency reached a 10-week high by the end of the session.
stories.i: The Indian Rupee gained 0.5% against the US dollar to hit a 10-week high. Foreign exchange inflows from overseas drove the strengthening of the local currency. The Reserve Bank of India also saw forex inflows support the move.
stories.a: The Indian Rupee appreciated 0.5% to touch a 10-week high against the US dollar. Substantial foreign inflows propelled the local unit upward during the session. Foreign exchange inflows managed by the Reserve Bank of India further reinforced the currency's upward trajectory.

stories.t: Central bank announces reverse repo auction
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India is the main bank that runs the country's money system. It announced a 3-day variable rate reverse repo auction. This auction will take place on September 4, 2026. The bank set the notified amount at 7,00,000 crore rupees.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled a 3-day variable rate reverse repo auction under the liquidity adjustment facility. The central bank set the notified amount at 7,00,000 crore rupees for September 4, 2026. Reversal of the transaction is scheduled for September 7, 2026.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India deployed a 3-day variable rate reverse repo auction through its liquidity adjustment facility. The central bank absorbed 7,00,000 crore rupees with a reversal date of September 7, 2026. This operation targets systemic liquidity management.

politics.b: Air India is receiving a rescue package from its owners worth 100 billion rupees.
politics.i: Air India secured a financial rescue package worth 100 billion rupees from its owners.
politics.a: Air India is slated to receive a 100 billion rupee financial injection from its parent owners.

timeline: Reserve Bank of India announces a 3-day variable rate reverse repo auction
Indian Rupee reaches a 10-week high following foreign exchange inflows

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras deals, CADE rulings, and Ibovespa pauses

stories.t: Petrobras and Petrochina Secure Spot Oil
stories.b: Petrobras and Petrochina each won five hundred thousand barrels of oil. They bought this fuel through Brazil's PPSA spot oil auction. PPSA is a state company that manages oil sharing contracts. An auction is a public sale where items go to the highest bidder. Both energy firms secured equal shares of the available petroleum.
stories.i: Petrobras and Petrochina secured five hundred thousand barrels of oil each in PPSA's spot oil auction. PPSA manages federal production-sharing agreements for offshore hydrocarbons. The state-run auction distributes state-owned crude to active refiners and traders. Both companies captured matching cargo allocations in the competitive tender process.
stories.a: Petrobras and Petrochina secured five hundred thousand barrels apiece in the latest PPSA spot tender. The federal state manager cleared two equal allocations from its pre-salt export supply. The spot auction clearing prices reflect current Brent-linked differentials for heavy sweet grades. Both entities integrated the new crude volumes into their regional refining logistics.

stories.t: Tribunal Rejects Petrobras Appeal on Merger
stories.b: Brazil's CADE Tribunal turned down an appeal from Petrobras. The appeal tried to block an approved merger between OceanPact and CBO. CADE is the government agency that checks company mergers for fair competition. The tribunal decided the corporate combination can proceed. Petrobras had asked them to review the decision.
stories.i: The CADE Tribunal dismissed an appeal filed by Petrobras regarding the OceanPact-CBO merger approval. CADE acts as Brazil's antitrust authority, overseeing market concentration and corporate consolidation. The tribunal upheld the clearance for the vessel operator combination. Petrobras contested the initial approval before the administrative body.
stories.a: The CADE Tribunal rejected the Petrobras administrative appeal challenging the OceanPact-CBO business combination clearance. Brazil's antitrust regulator sustained its original competition assessment despite objections from the state oil producer. The ruling allows the maritime support service providers to proceed with corporate integration. The decision exhausts standard administrative remedies for opposing stakeholders within the agency.

stories.t: Ibovespa Snaps Winning Streak
stories.b: The Ibovespa stock index finished the day flat. An index is a group of stocks tracked together to show how a market is doing. This flat finish followed a winning streak that lasted for eleven straight sessions. Stocks across the board stopped climbing for a single day. Traders watched the main market gauge pause its upward run.
stories.i: The Ibovespa closed flat following an eleven-session winning streak. The benchmark equity index paused its prolonged upward trajectory after continuous daily gains. Trading volume absorbed standard profit-taking across key sector components. Local equities consolidated recent advances without posting directional losses.
stories.a: The Ibovespa settled unchanged, terminating an eleven-session consecutive rally. The benchmark index exhausted short-term buying pressure as market participants locked in multi-session gains. Sectoral rotation neutralized minor downward impulses across heavyweight index constituents. Price action established a temporary plateau following weeks of uninterrupted upward momentum.

politics.b: Kanczuk suggested changes for Copom inflation forecasts. Copom is the committee that sets interest rates in Brazil. Inflation means prices rise and money buys less over time. The proposals aim to improve how the bank predicts future price changes.
politics.i: Kanczuk presented proposed modifications for Copom forecasting models. Copom functions as the monetary policy committee determining the benchmark Selic rate. The suggested adjustments target estimation errors in official price projections. Central bank researchers evaluate methodology changes to enhance policy transmission.
politics.a: Kanczuk published methodological adjustments targeting Copom inflation forecasting frameworks. The policy proposals address systemic deviations in central bank forward-looking price models. Improved estimation accuracy directly impacts the interest rate path priced into swap curves. Market participants monitor potential parameter changes for signals on future monetary tightening cycles.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Oil demand forecasts and Aramco partnerships

stories.t: OPEC Adjusts Demand Predictions While Aramco Expands Technology Alliances
stories.b: OPEC lowered its global oil demand forecast for the second quarter due to the Iran war. OPEC also cut its growth forecast for global oil demand in 2026. Meanwhile, Saudi Aramco signed an industrial artificial intelligence partnership with Avathon and an MOU with Quantinuum to explore quantum computing.
stories.i: OPEC lowered its second-quarter global oil demand forecast following the Iran war, alongside a broader reduction to its 2026 global oil demand growth forecast. In domestic corporate developments, Saudi Aramco established an industrial artificial intelligence partnership with Avathon and signed a memorandum of understanding with Quantinuum to explore industrial quantum computing.
stories.a: OPEC reduced its second-quarter demand projections amid the Iran war and downgraded 2026 growth forecasts. Concurrently, Saudi Aramco diversified its technological capabilities through an industrial AI partnership with Avathon and a quantum computing memorandum of understanding with Quantinuum.

stories.t: Refinery Incident and OPEC Production Dynamics
stories.b: Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery was struck by a drone. Meanwhile, sources indicated that OPEC+ is likely to raise oil output targets again starting in September. HSBC reported that the UAE's departure from OPEC will have a limited near-term impact, and former President Trump welcomed the exit.
stories.i: A drone struck Aramco's Ras Tanura refinery. Sources reported that OPEC+ will likely raise its oil output targets again from September. HSBC analysts noted that the UAE's departure from OPEC carries a limited near-term impact, while Donald Trump welcomed the exit.
stories.a: A drone strike hit Aramco's Ras Tanura facility as market participants weighed expectations that OPEC+ will lift output targets from September. HSBC observed limited near-term structural impact from the UAE's exit from OPEC, an exit publicly welcomed by Donald Trump.

politics.b: Donald Trump welcomed the United Arab Emirates leaving OPEC. No other political statements were recorded.
politics.i: Donald Trump publicly welcomed the departure of the United Arab Emirates from OPEC.
politics.a: Former President Donald Trump publicly welcomed the United Arab Emirates' exit from OPEC.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira appreciation, reserves growth, and index inclusion

stories.t: Naira Reaches Two-Year High Amid Subsidy Shifts
stories.b: The national currency of Nigeria climbed to N1,315.67 per dollar. This marks its highest level in two years and puts it on track for its biggest annual gain since 2018. Currency stability has been helped by the removal of fuel subsidies and an increase in local refining. Foreign exchange reserves also grew to $53.99bn.
stories.i: The Nigerian currency strengthened to a two-year high of N1,315.67 per dollar, heading for its strongest annual performance since 2018. NARTO credited the currency stability to fuel subsidy removal and domestic petroleum refining. Meanwhile, foreign exchange reserves expanded to $53.99bn.
stories.a: The naira advanced to N1,315.67 per dollar, extending a trajectory toward its strongest annual appreciation since 2018. Market participants attribute the sustained currency stability to structural adjustments from fuel subsidy removal alongside domestic refining capacity. Concurrently, gross foreign exchange reserves reached $53.99bn, reinforcing external buffers.

stories.t: FTSE Russell Adds Nigerian Equities Ahead of Frontier Return
stories.b: FTSE Russell added 31 Nigerian stocks to its index. This comes ahead of the country returning to frontier market status. Stock indices track groups of companies so investors can measure market performance easily.
stories.i: FTSE Russell included 31 Nigerian stocks in its index ahead of the market's return to frontier status. Index inclusion typically alters passive capital flows as funds tracking the benchmark adjust their portfolios.
stories.a: FTSE Russell integrated 31 Nigerian equities into its index ahead of the market's reclassification to frontier status. The inclusion alters passive tracking mandates and mandates rebalancing among institutional investors benchmarking against the index.

politics.b: The Defence Minister justified a 5.41 trillion naira security allocation in the 2026 budget. A minister is a government official in charge of a specific department. Separately, a minister stated that the Nigerian economy has stabilised following reforms to fuel subsidies.
politics.i: The Defence Minister defended the 5.41 trillion naira security allocation within the 2026 budget. Meanwhile, a government official stated that the economy has achieved stability following recent subsidy reforms.
politics.a: The Defence Minister defended the 5.41 trillion naira security allocation outlined in the 2026 budget. Concurrently, ministerial commentary maintained that the broader economy has achieved stability following the implementation of fiscal subsidy reforms.

timeline: FTSE Russell adds 31 Nigerian stocks to index ahead of frontier return.
Naira reaches a two-year high of N1,315.67 as reserves hit $53.99bn.
Defence Minister justifies 5.41 trillion naira security allocation in the 2026 budget.

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Australian dollar rises and corporate capital updates emerge

stories.t: Australian Dollar Reaches Four-Month High Amid Rate Expectations
stories.b: The money in Australia, called the Australian dollar, went up in value. It reached a four-month high against other currencies. Traders think the central bank, which sets the cost of borrowing money, might raise interest rates. These are the fees charged on loans. This shift changed how currency traders view the market.
stories.i: The Australian dollar touched a four-month peak. Changing expectations around monetary policy drove the move. Traders increased their bets on potential rate hikes from the central bank. This shift in risk sentiment boosted the currency across major pairs.
stories.a: The Australian dollar printed a four-month high. Repricing of terminal rate risks drove the move as market participants adjusted rate-hike probabilities. This hawkish repricing tightened yield differentials against major trading partners.

stories.t: Andromeda Metals Secures Funds for Alumina Project
stories.b: A company named Andromeda Metals collected $3.04 million in funding. The business plans to use the money for a high-purity alumina project. Alumina is a material used in various industrial products. This capital raise helps the firm advance its operations.
stories.i: Andromeda Metals raised $3.04 million in fresh capital. The firm allocated the proceeds to advance its high-purity alumina project. Corporate fundraising in the materials sector continues to support early-stage development milestones.
stories.a: Andromeda Metals completed a $3.04 million capital raise. Proceeds target the advancement of its high-purity alumina development pipeline. Equity issuance conditions for junior miners remain selective.

politics.b: No government policy updates were reported for Australian financial markets today.
politics.i: No fiscal or regulatory policy updates influenced Australian markets in this session.
politics.a: No sovereign policy announcements impacted pricing during this session.

timeline: Andromeda Metals raises $3.04 million for its alumina project.
The Australian dollar reaches a four-month high on rate expectations.
